newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan tenders for 50,000 T sugar for Sept.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan tenders for 50,000 T sugar for Sept.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said on Monday it had tendered for 50,000 tonnes of crystal white refined sugar to be delivered in Karachi by September 30.
The tender notice said shipment was required in full shiploads of 12,500 tonnes each. Bids should be submitted by 0600 GMT on August 31 for immediate opening.
A TCP official said on Thursday the TCP had an option with an Indian firm to deliver 75,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar in September at $389 per tonne C & F Karachi.
The TCP has already booked 225,000 tonnes of sugar for delivery by August 31.

Dealers and industry sources said Pakistan would need to import more to cover an expected shortfall in October and November in the absence of carried over stocks. Last year there were carried over stocks of 400,000 tonnes.

The Food and Agriculture Ministry had asked the TCP to import 225,000 tonnes by September to halt a rise in domestic prices and offset lower domestic output of 2.47 million tonnes in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) against 3.0 million in 1994/95.
The TCP has bought a total of 175,000 tonnes from the ISGI, 25,000 tonnes from a Turkish firm and another 25,000 tonnes from a Brazilian firm, all of it due to reach Pakistan by August 31.
The TCP official said a consigment of 12,000 tonnes of white sugar from India bought by a private firm at $394 per tonne C&F was likely to reach Karachi port in the next few days.
The private Pakistan Sugar Mills Association (PSMA) said mills had stocks of about 300,000 tonnes on August 15.
